threads.body: Both callers (`release-package.yml` and `release-all.yml`) invoke this reusable workflow with only `contents: read`. A reusable workflow cannot elevate its caller's token permissions, so the new write permissions prevent these build calls from running. Add `id-token: write` and `attestations: write`, alongside `contents: read`, to both callers' `build` jobs.

threads.body: The provenance action derives its source commit from the workflow's OIDC `sha` claim, not from checkout HEAD or `built_sha`. The single-package path still checks out the mutable `github.ref`: if the branch advances between dispatch and checkout, artifacts can be built from commit B while their signed provenance identifies commit A. Default checkout to `github.sha` and reject explicit refs whose resolved commit differs from the attested source SHA.

threads.body: This exposes `built_sha` only as an internal job output. Without an `on.workflow_call.outputs` mapping, `needs.build.outputs.built_sha` in `release-package.yml` is empty, so finalization falls back to the mutable `github.ref`. A merge during publishing can therefore still make the release tag point at a different commit from the artifacts. Export the job output through the reusable workflow's interface.

threads.body: The three-day cutoff applies only to this version-validation subprocess. Both subsequent `uv build` commands resolve isolated build dependencies without it, including the unpinned `hatchling` backend. A newly published build backend can therefore execute during release despite the dependency-age protection described in the PR. Export `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER=3d` so both builds inherit the cutoff.

threads.body:
With `id-token: write` here, any build dependency (hatchling, etc.) can mint an OIDC token. PyPI accepts that token for publishing unless the trusted publisher is restricted to the `pypi` environment, which this job doesn't use. Could you confirm the PyPI trusted publisher config has the `pypi` environment set? If not, it'd be good to set it.

Optionally, [dotnet-instrumentation attests in a separate job](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet-instrumentation/blob/5c59b4a5088c418e2b29826abc99e30e92ae1630/.github/workflows/release.yml#L34-L42) after downloading the artifacts, so the build job doesn't need `id-token` at all.

threads.body:
Suggest dropping the merged-PR check. It doesn't add protection beyond the branch check above: [`commits/{sha}/pulls`](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits#list-pull-requests-associated-with-a-commit) returns the PR that introduced any commit on `main`, so every commit on a protected branch passes. Branch protection / rulesets on `main` and `package-release/*` already cover this, and no other OTel repo does an extra check like this.

